note: Mixed layout: the top third is two columns (Example 7.8, left column first), and below it a full-page-width blue SUMMARY panel. previous_page_last_block was null, but I read page 12 of this chapter directly before: it ended with the complete sentence '...hence their energies cannot be positive or zero.', and this page opens with a new Example 7.8 box, so first_block_continues_from_previous is false on that evidence. The SUMMARY panel is cut off by the page end in the middle of item 4 (only sub-item (a) is printed; (b) and the rest continue overleaf), so last_block_continues_on_next is true. On the summary panel: the agent rule says a box is its own block, but this panel contains four numbered display equations that must be left to the special transcriber, so I broke it into its 'SUMMARY' heading, its numbered/lettered items as list blocks and its display equations as needs_special equation blocks rather than flattening equations into one box of text. Marked needs_special with pixel bboxes (original 1826x2167): the E_i display (n=3), the E_f display (n=5), the '(delta)E = E_f - E_i' line (n=7), the two-line numerical computation ending '= 3.13 x 10^9 J' (n=8), the '(delta)V = V_f - V_i = -6.25 x 10^9 J' line (n=11), and inside the summary F = Gm_1m_2/r^2 (n=14), the F_R summation with its sigma from i=1 to n (n=17), T^2 = (4(pi)^2/GM_s)R^3 (n=24) and the two-line g(h) expression with its 'for h << R_E' tail (n=28). Notation discrepancies: the text layer flattens every subscript and superscript (image prints R_E, M_E, E_i, E_f, K_f, K_i, V_f, V_i, m_1, m_2, M_1, M_2, M_n, F_1, F_2, F_n, F_R, M_s, R_E^2, r^2, R^3, T^2, 10^6, 10^9, 10^-11, N m^2 kg^-2) and destroys fractions, the summation sign's limits and the radical-free structure of the displays; the inline flat forms kept in blocks n=1, n=9, n=15, n=16 and n=25 must have their notation read from the image. Greek capital delta appears in the text layer as '∆' (increment sign) where the image prints an upright Greek Delta in (delta)E, (delta)K and (delta)V, and the summation symbol is given as 'Σ' in block n=18, matching the image's quoted sigma. The small triangular markers at the Example 7.8 box edges are box decoration, not text.
